1. Core Clinical Tension: A 17-year-old Tunisian male presented with a tender, warm, erythematous popliteal mass and knee flexion stance, accompanied by weight loss, fever, night sweats, and ipsilateral saphenous thrombophlebitis. The acute inflammatory signs and regional thrombophlebitis closely mimicked an acute pyogenic abscess, infected Baker's cyst, soft-tissue sarcoma, or musculoskeletal brucellosis (encouraged by raw milk consumption).
2. Admission Breakpoint: Following physical examination, inflammatory laboratory workup, plain radiographs, Doppler ultrasound, and contrast MRI defining the popliteal cystic mass and saphenous thrombophlebitis, immediately prior to serological testing, cultures, and ultrasound-guided biopsy puncture.
3. Differential Distinctions: Musculoskeletal brucellosis (promoted by unpasteurized dairy consumption in Tunisia), acute pyogenic bacterial abscess / infected synovial cyst, and soft-tissue sarcoma. Differentiated by negative Brucella serology (Rose Bengal/Wright), sterile bacterial cultures, and histopathology showing epithelioid granulation tissue with acellular eosinophilic necrosis.
case_prompt: A 17-year-old male high school student from central-western Tunisia presented with a painful, red, hot swelling in the right popliteal fossa that was resistant to first-line analgesic therapy. He reported an intentional weight loss of 5 kilograms over the past 2 months, along with daily fevers and nocturnal sweats over the past 2 weeks. He had household contact with a sibling treated for a chronic pulmonary infection 7 years prior and endorsed regular consumption of unpasteurized milk. On physical examination, the patient walked with an antalgic limp due to a knee flexion posture (knee flessum). A tender, warm, erythematous, soft, and mobile mass measuring 10 cm in diameter was palpable in the right popliteal fossa, with an enlarged ipsilateral inguinal lymph node. There was no knee joint effusion and no bone tenderness over the distal femur or proximal tibia. Laboratory tests revealed a white blood cell count of 12,040/μL and a C-reactive protein level of 67.3 mg/L. Plain radiographs of the chest and right knee were normal. Doppler ultrasound of the lower limb demonstrated a fluid collection in the right popliteal fossa with internal echoes, a well-defined wall independent of the popliteal vascular pedicle, and thrombophlebitis of the right saphenous vein. Contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated an 8 cm well-vascularized, partly liquefied mass developing adjacent to the semimembranosus and medial gastrocnemius muscles, popliteal vessels, and posterior tibial nerve, accompanied by muscular and adipose edema and popliteal lymphadenopathy, without synovial effusion or bony signal abnormality.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: High initial suspicion given frequent consumption of unpasteurized milk in rural Tunisia, systemic constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), and a localized inflammatory mass; ruled out by negative serological testing.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: negative Rose Bengal serology and negative Wright serology.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial abscess / infected popliteal cyst
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the warm, erythematous, tender presentation with elevated inflammatory markers and regional thrombophlebitis; ruled out by negative bacteriological evaluation of aspirate material and chronic granulomatous rather than purulent histology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: An ultrasound-guided biopsy puncture was done. The bacteriological results were negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Histopathological examination of tissue obtained via ultrasound-guided biopsy puncture demonstrated inflammatory granulation tissue with epithelioid cells and acellular eosinophil deposits characteristic of a tuberculous origin.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histopathological examination revealed the presence of inflammatory granulation tissue with acellular eosinophil deposits and epithelioid cells, suggesting a tuberculous origin ( Figure 5).

editor_comments: Distilled case accurately preserves admission triage up to Doppler/MRI imaging, preceding biopsy and serologies. Quotes verified.
